output.summary: A prostrate flowering succulent endemic to eastern Australia, angular sea-fig usually grows very close to the sea. It has blue-grey leaves, daisy-like light-purple to deep pinkish-purple flowers, and red to purple fruit that ripens mainly in summer and autumn.
output.edibilityNote: Aboriginal peoples ate the fruit; the fleshy leaves may be eaten raw or cooked, and roasted leaves can serve as a salt substitute.
